Locally redefining color spaces within the same layer could\n    be confusing, so that practice is discouraged.\n\n    The default color space values are equivalent to an identity transform, so\n    applying this schema and invoking `UsdColorSpaceAPI::ComputeColorSpace()`\n    on a prim resolving to a defaulted color definition will return a color\n    space equivalent to the identity transform.\n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n    float2 colorSpaceDefinition:__INSTANCE_NAME__:blueChroma = (0, 0) (\n        doc = \"Blue chromaticity coordinates\"\n    )\n    float colorSpaceDefinition:__INSTANCE_NAME__:gamma = 1 (\n        doc = \"Gamma value of the log section\"\n    )\n    float2 colorSpaceDefinition:__INSTANCE_NAME__:greenChroma = (0, 1) (\n        doc = \"Green chromaticity coordinates\"\n    )\n    float colorSpaceDefinition:__INSTANCE_NAME__:linearBias = 0 (\n        doc = \"Linear bias of the log section\"\n    )\n    uniform token colorSpaceDefinition:__INSTANCE_NAME__:name = \"custom\" (\n        doc = \"\"\"The name of the color space defined on this prim.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    float2 colorSpaceDefinition:__INSTANCE_NAME__:redChroma = (1, 0) (\n        doc = \"Red chromaticity coordinates\"\n    )\n    float2 colorSpaceDefinition:__INSTANCE_NAME__:whitePoint = (0.33333334, 0.33333334) (\n        doc = \"Whitepoint chromaticity coordinates\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"CollectionAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"A general purpose API schema used to describe a collection of prims\n    and properties within a scene. This API schema can be applied to a prim\n    multiple times with different instance names to define several collections\n    on a single prim.\n\n    A collection's membership is specified one of two ways. The first way uses\n    the built-in relationships `includes` and `excludes`, and the attribute\n    `includeRoot` to determine membership. The second way is termed a\n    pattern-based collection, and uses the built-in attribute\n    `membershipExpression` to determine membership. Here we will refer to\n    collections using `includes`, `excludes` and `includeRoot` as being in\n    *relationship-mode* and those using the `membershipExpression` as being in\n    *expression-mode*.\n\n    A collection is determined to be in *relationship-mode* when either or both\n    of its `includes` and `excludes` relationships have valid targets, or the\n    `includeRoot` attribute is set `true`.  In this case, the pattern-based\n    `membershipExpression` attribute is ignored.  Otherwise, the collection is\n    in *expression-mode* and the `membershipExpression` attribute applies.\n\n    In *relationship-mode* the `includes` and `excludes` relationships specify\n    the collection members as a set of paths to include and a set of paths to\n    exclude.  Whether or not the descendants of an included path belong to a\n    collection is decided by its expansion rule (see below).  If the collection\n    excludes paths that are not descendent to included paths, the collection\n    implicitly includes the root path `</>`.  If such a collection also\n    includes paths that are not descendent to the excluded paths, it is\n    considered invalid since the intent is ambiguous.\n\n    In *expression-mode*, the pattern-based `membershipExpression` attribute is\n    used with the `expansionRule` attribute to determine collection membership.\n    See the detailed descriptions of the built-in properties below for more\n    details.\n\n    Collection API Properties\n\n    The built-in properties for this schema are in the `collection:instanceName`\n    namespace, where `instanceName` is the user-provided applied API schema\n    instance name.\n\n    <ul>\n    <li>`uniform token collection:instanceName:expansionRule` - in\n    *relationship-mode*, specifies how to expand the `includes` and `excludes`\n    relationship targets to determine the collection's members.  In\n    *expression-mode*, specifies how matching scene objects against the\n    `membershipExpression` proceeds.  Possible values include:\n        <ul>\n        <li>`expandPrims` - in *relationship-mode*, all the prims descendent\n        to the `includes` relationship targets (and not descendent to `excludes`\n        relationship targets) belong to the collection.  Any `includes`-targeted\n        property paths also belong to the collection. This is the default\n        behavior. In *expression-mode*, the functions\n        UsdComputeIncludedObjectsFromCollection() and\n        UsdComputeIncludedPathsFromCollection() only test prims against the\n        `membershipExpression` to determine membership.\n        </li>\n        <li>`expandPrimsAndProperties` - like `expandPrims`, but in\n        *relationship-mode*, all properties on all included prims also belong to\n        the collection. In *expression-mode*, the functions\n        UsdComputeIncludedObjectsFromCollection() and\n        UsdComputeIncludedPathsFromCollection() test both prims and\n        properties against the `membershipExpression` to determine membership.\n        </li>\n        <li>`explicitOnly` - in *relationship-mode*, only paths in the\n        `includes` relationship targets and not those in the `excludes`\n        relationship targets belong to the collection. Does not apply to\n        *expression-mode*. If set in *expression-mode*, the functions\n        UsdComputeIncludedObjectsFromCollection() and\n        UsdComputeIncludedPathsFromCollection() return no results.\n        </li>\n        </ul>\n        </li>\n\n    <li>`bool collection:instanceName:includeRoot` - boolean attribute\n    indicating whether the pseudo-root path `</>` should be counted as one\n    of the included target paths in *relationship-mode*. This separate attribute\n    is required because relationships cannot directly target the root. When\n    `expansionRule` is `explicitOnly`, this attribute is ignored. The fallback\n    value is false. When set to `true`, this collection is in\n    *relationship-mode*. This attribute is ignored in *expression-mode*.  </li>\n\n    <li>`rel collection:instanceName:includes` - in *relationship-mode*,\n    specifies a list of targets that are included in the collection. This can\n    target prims or properties directly. A collection can insert the rules of\n    another collection by making its `includes` relationship target the\n    `collection:otherInstanceName` property from the collection to be included\n    (see UsdCollectionAPI::GetCollectionAttr).  Note that including another\n    collection does not guarantee the contents of that collection will be in the\n    final collection; instead, the rules are merged.  This means, for example,\n    an exclude entry may exclude a portion of the included collection.  When a\n    collection includes one or more collections, the order in which targets are\n    added to the includes relationship may become significant, if there are\n    conflicting opinions about the same path. Targets that are added later are\n    considered to be stronger than earlier targets for the same path.  This\n    relationship is ignored in *expression-mode*.</li>\n\n    <li>`rel collection:instanceName:excludes` - in *relationship-mode*,\n    specifies a list of targets that are excluded below the <b>included</b>\n    paths in this collection. This can target prims or properties directly, but\n    <b>cannot target another collection</b>. This is to keep the membership\n    determining logic simple, efficient and easier to reason about. Finally, it\n    is invalid for a collection to exclude paths that are not included in\n    it. The presence of such \\\"orphaned\\\" excluded paths will not affect the set\n    of paths included in the collection, but may affect the performance of\n    querying membership of a path in the collection (see\n    UsdCollectionMembershipQuery::IsPathIncluded) or of enumerating the\n    objects belonging to the collection (see\n    UsdCollectionAPI::ComputeIncludedObjects).  This relationship is ignored in\n    *expression-mode*.</li>\n\n    <li>`uniform opaque collection:instanceName` - opaque\n    attribute (meaning it can never have a value) that represents the collection\n    for the purpose of allowing another collection to include it in\n    *relationship-mode*. When this property is targeted by another collection's\n    `includes` relationship, the rules of this collection will be inserted\n    into the rules of the collection that includes it.</li>\n\n    <li>`uniform pathExpression collection:instanceName:membershipExpression` -\n    in *expression-mode*, defines the SdfPathExpression used to test\n    objects for collection membership.</li>\n\n    </ul>\n\n    \\\\subsection usd_collectionapi_implicit_inclusion Implicit Inclusion\n\n    In some scenarios it is useful to express a collection that includes\n    everything except certain paths.  To support this, a *relationship-mode*\n    collection that has an exclude that is not descendent to any include will\n    include the root path `</>`.\n\n    Creating Collections in C++\n    \n    \\\\snippet examples_usd.cpp ApplyCollections\n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n    uniform opaque collection:__INSTANCE_NAME__ (\n        doc = \"\"\"This property represents the collection for the purpose of \n        allowing another collection to include it. When this property is \n        targeted by another collection's <i>includes</i> relationship, the rules\n        of this collection will be inserted into the rules of the collection\n        that includes it.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    rel collection:__INSTANCE_NAME__:excludes (\n        doc = '''Specifies a list of targets that are excluded below\n        the included paths in this collection. This can target prims or\n        properties directly, but cannot target another collection. This is to\n        keep the membership determining logic simple, efficient and easier to\n        reason about. Finally, it is invalid for a collection to exclude\n        paths that are not included in it. The presence of such \"orphaned\"\n        excluded paths will not affect the set of paths included in the\n        collection, but may affect the performance of querying membership of \n        a path in the collection (see\n        UsdCollectionAPI::MembershipQuery::IsPathIncluded) \n        or of enumerating the objects belonging to the collection (see \n        UsdCollectionAPI::GetIncludedObjects).'''\n    )\n    uniform token collection:__INSTANCE_NAME__:expansionRule = \"expandPrims\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"explicitOnly\", \"expandPrims\", \"expandPrimsAndProperties\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Specifies how the paths that are included in\n        the collection must be expanded to determine its members.\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform bool collection:__INSTANCE_NAME__:includeRoot (\n        doc = \"\"\"Boolean attribute indicating whether the pseudo-root\n        path `</>` should be counted as one of the included target\n        paths.  The fallback is false.  This separate attribute is\n        required because relationships cannot directly target the root.\"\"\"\n    )\n    rel collection:__INSTANCE_NAME__:includes (\n        doc = \"\"\"Specifies a list of targets that are included in the collection.\n        This can target prims or properties directly. A collection can insert\n        the rules of another collection by making its <i>includes</i>\n        relationship target the <b>collection:{collectionName}</b> property on\n        the owning prim of the collection to be included\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform pathExpression collection:__INSTANCE_NAME__:membershipExpression (\n        doc = \"\"\"Specifies a path expression that determines membership in this\n        collection.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"ClipsAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\" UsdClipsAPI is an API schema that provides an interface to\n    a prim's clip metadata. Clips are a \\\"value resolution\\\" feature that \n    allows one to specify a sequence of usd files (clips) to be consulted, \n    over time, as a source of varying overrides for the prims at and \n    beneath this prim in namespace.\n            \n    SetClipAssetPaths() establishes the set of clips that can be consulted.\n    SetClipActive() specifies the ordering of clip application over time \n    (clips can be repeated), while SetClipTimes() specifies time-mapping\n    from stage-time to clip-time for the clip active at a given stage-time,\n    which allows for time-dilation and repetition of clips. \n    Finally, SetClipPrimPath() determines the path within each clip that will \n    map to this prim, i.e. the location within the clip at which we will look\n    for opinions for this prim. \n\n    The clip asset paths, times and active metadata can also be specified \n    through template clip metadata. This can be desirable when your set of \n    assets is very large, as the template metadata is much more concise. \n    SetClipTemplateAssetPath() establishes the asset identifier pattern of the \n    set of clips to be consulted. SetClipTemplateStride(), \n    SetClipTemplateEndTime(), and SetClipTemplateStartTime() specify the range \n    in which USD will search, based on the template. From the set of resolved \n    asset paths, times and active will be derived internally.\n\n    A prim may have multiple \\\"clip sets\\\" -- named sets of clips that each\n    have their own values for the metadata described above. For example, \n    a prim might have a clip set named \\\"Clips_1\\\" that specifies some group\n    of clip asset paths, and another clip set named \\\"Clips_2\\\" that uses\n    an entirely different set of clip asset paths. These clip sets are \n    composed across composition arcs, so clip sets for a prim may be\n    defined in multiple sublayers or references, for example. Individual\n    metadata for a given clip set may be sparsely overridden.\n                \n    Important facts about clips:            \n    - Within the layerstack in which clips are established, the           \n    opinions within the clips will be weaker than any local opinions\n    in the layerstack, but em stronger than varying opinions coming across\n    references and variants.            \n    - We will never look for metadata or default opinions in clips            \n    when performing value resolution on the owning stage, since these           \n    quantities must be time-invariant.          \n            \n    This leads to the common structure in which we reference a model asset\n    on a prim, and then author clips at the same site: the asset reference\n    will provide the topology and unvarying data for the model, while the \n    clips will provide the time-sampled animation.\n\n    For further information, see \\\\ref Usd_Page_ValueClips\n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n}\n\n"
- "#usda 1.0\n(\n    \"WARNING: THIS FILE IS GENERATED BY usdGenSchema.  DO NOT EDIT.\"\n)\n\nclass GenerativeProcedural \"GenerativeProcedural\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"\n    Represents an abstract generative procedural prim which delivers its input\n    parameters via properties (including relationships) within the \\\"primvars:\\\"\n    namespace.\n \n    It does not itself have any awareness or participation in the execution of\n    the procedural but rather serves as a means of delivering a procedural's\n    definition and input parameters.\n \n    The value of its \\\"proceduralSystem\\\" property (either authored or provided\n    by API schema fallback) indicates to which system the procedural definition\n    is meaningful.\n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n    float3[] extent (\n        doc = \"\"\"Extent is a three dimensional range measuring the geometric\n        extent of the authored gprim in its own local space (i.e. its own\n        transform not applied), without accounting for any shader-induced\n        displacement. If __any__ extent value has been authored for a given \n        Boundable, then it should be authored at every timeSample at which \n        geometry-affecting properties are authored, to ensure correct \n        evaluation via ComputeExtent(). If __no__ extent value has been \n        authored, then ComputeExtent() will call the Boundable's registered \n        ComputeExtentFunction(), which may be expensive, which is why we \n        strongly encourage proper authoring of extent.\n        \\\\sa ComputeExtent()\n        \\\\sa \\\\ref UsdGeom_Boundable_Extent.\n        \n        An authored extent on a prim which has children is expected to include\n        the extent of all children, as they will be pruned from BBox computation\n        during traversal.\"\"\"\n    )\n    token proceduralSystem (\n        doc = \"\"\"The name or convention of the system responsible for evaluating\n        the procedural.\n        NOTE: A fallback value for this is typically set via an API schema.\"\"\"\n    )\n    rel proxyPrim (\n        doc = '''The proxyPrim relationship allows us to link a\n        prim whose purpose is \"render\" to its (single target)\n        purpose=\"proxy\" prim.  This is entirely optional, but can be\n        useful in several scenarios:\n        \n        - In a pipeline that does pruning (for complexity management)\n        by deactivating prims composed from asset references, when we\n        deactivate a purpose=\"render\" prim, we will be able to discover\n        and additionally deactivate its associated purpose=\"proxy\" prim,\n        so that preview renders reflect the pruning accurately.\n        \n        - DCC importers may be able to make more aggressive optimizations\n        for interactive processing and display if they can discover the proxy\n        for a given render prim.\n        \n        - With a little more work, a Hydra-based application will be able\n        to map a picked proxy prim back to its render geometry for selection.\n\n        \\\\note It is only valid to author the proxyPrim relationship on\n        prims whose purpose is \"render\".'''\n    )\n    uniform token purpose = \"default\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"default\", \"render\", \"proxy\", \"guide\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Purpose is a classification of geometry into categories that \n        can each be independently included or excluded from traversals of prims \n        on a stage, such as rendering or bounding-box computation traversals.\n\n        See for more detail about how \n        purpose is computed and used.\"\"\"\n    )\n    token visibility = \"inherited\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"inherited\", \"invisible\"]\n        doc = '''Visibility is meant to be the simplest form of \"pruning\" \n        visibility that is supported by most DCC apps.  Visibility is \n        animatable, allowing a sub-tree of geometry to be present for some \n        segment of a shot, and absent from others; unlike the action of \n        deactivating geometry prims, invisible geometry is still \n        available for inspection, for positioning, for defining volumes, etc.'''\n    )\n    uniform token[] xformOpOrder (\n        doc = \"\"\"Encodes the sequence of transformation operations in the\n        order in which they should be pushed onto a transform stack while\n        visiting a UsdStage's prims in a graph traversal that will effect\n        the desired positioning for this prim and its descendant prims.\n        \n        You should rarely, if ever, need to manipulate this attribute directly.\n        It is managed by the AddXformOp(), SetResetXformStack(), and\n        SetXformOpOrder(), and consulted by GetOrderedXformOps() and\n        GetLocalTransformation().\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\n"
- "#usda 1.0\n(\n    \"WARNING: THIS FILE IS GENERATED BY usdGenSchema.  DO NOT EDIT.\"\n)\n\nclass NodeGraph \"NodeGraph\" (\n    doc = '''A node-graph is a container for shading nodes, as well as other \n    node-graphs. It has a public input interface and provides a list of public \n    outputs.\n\n    <b>Node Graph Interfaces</b>\n    \n    One of the most important functions of a node-graph is to host the \"interface\"\n    with which clients of already-built shading networks will interact.  Please\n    see \"Interface Inputs\" for a detailed\n    explanation of what the interface provides, and how to construct and\n    use it, to effectively share/instance shader networks.\n\n    <b>Node Graph Outputs</b>\n\n    These behave like outputs on a shader and are typically connected to an \n    output on a shader inside the node-graph.\n    '''\n)\n{\n}\n\nclass Material \"Material\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"A Material provides a container into which multiple \\\"render contexts\\\"\n    can add data that defines a \\\"shading material\\\" for a renderer. Typically \n    this consists of one or more UsdShadeOutput properties connected to outputs \n    of nested Shader prims - though a context/client is free to add\n    any data that is suitable. We <b>strongly advise</b> that all contexts\n    adopt the convention that all properties be prefixed with a namespace\n    that identifies the context e.g. \\\"token outputs:ri:surface.connect = \n    </MyselfMaterial/previewSurface.outputs:surface\\\". \n    \n    ## Binding Materials\n    \n    In the UsdShading model, geometry expresses a binding to a single Material or\n    to a set of Materials partitioned by UsdGeomSubsets defined beneath the\n    geometry; it is legal to bind a Material at the root (or other sub-prim) of \n    a model, and then bind a different Material to individual gprims, but the\n    meaning of inheritance and \\\"ancestral overriding\\\" of Material bindings is \n    left to each render-target to determine.  Since UsdGeom has no concept of \n    shading, we provide the API for binding and unbinding geometry on the API \n    schema UsdShadeMaterialBindingAPI.\n    \n    ## Material Variation\n    \n    The entire power of USD VariantSets and all the other composition \n    operators can leveraged when encoding shading variation.  \n    UsdShadeMaterial provides facilities for a particular way of building\n    \\\"Material variants\\\" in which neither the identity of the Materials themselves\n    nor the geometry Material-bindings need to change - instead we vary the\n    targeted networks, interface values, and even parameter values within\n    a single variantSet.  \n    See \\\"Authoring Material Variations\\\" \n    for more details.\n\n    ## Materials Encapsulate their Networks in Namespace\n    \n    UsdShade requires that all of the shaders that \\\"belong\\\" to the Material \n    live under the Material in namespace. This supports powerful, easy reuse\n    of Materials, because it allows us to *reference* a Material from one\n    asset (the asset might be a library of Materials) into another asset: USD \n    references compose all descendant prims of the reference target into the \n    referencer's namespace, which means that all of the referenced Material's \n    shader networks will come along with the Material. When referenced in this\n    way, Materials can also be [instanced](http://openusd.org/docs/USD-Glossary.html#USDGlossary-Instancing), for ease of deduplication and compactness.\n    Finally, Material encapsulation also allows us to \n    \\\"specialize\\\" child materials from \n    parent materials.\n    \n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n    token outputs:displacement (\n        displayGroup = \"Outputs\"\n        doc = '''Represents the universal \"displacement\" output terminal of a \n        material.'''\n    )\n    token outputs:surface (\n        displayGroup = \"Outputs\"\n        doc = '''Represents the universal \"surface\" output terminal of a\n        material.'''\n    )\n    token outputs:volume (\n        displayGroup = \"Outputs\"\n        doc = '''Represents the universal \"volume\" output terminal of a\n        material.'''\n    )\n}\n\nclass Shader \"Shader\" (\n    apiSchemas = [\"NodeDefAPI\"]\n    doc = '''Base class for all USD shaders. Shaders are the building blocks\n    of shading networks. While UsdShadeShader objects are not target specific,\n    each renderer or application target may derive its own renderer-specific \n    shader object types from this base, if needed.\n    \n    Objects of this class generally represent a single shading object, whether\n    it exists in the target renderer or not. For example, a texture, a fractal,\n    or a mix node.\n\n    The UsdShadeNodeDefAPI provides attributes to uniquely identify the\n    type of this node.  The id resolution into a renderable shader target\n    type of this node.  The id resolution into a renderable shader target\n    is deferred to the consuming application.\n\n    The purpose of representing them in Usd is two-fold:\n    - To represent, via \"connections\" the topology of the shading network\n    that must be reconstructed in the renderer. Facilities for authoring and \n    manipulating connections are encapsulated in the API schema \n    UsdShadeConnectableAPI.\n    - To present a (partial or full) interface of typed input parameters \n    whose values can be set and overridden in Usd, to be provided later at \n    render-time as parameter values to the actual render shader objects. Shader \n    input parameters are encapsulated in the property schema UsdShadeInput.\n    '''\n)\n{\n}\n\nclass \"NodeDefAPI\" (\n    doc = '''UsdShadeNodeDefAPI is an API schema that provides attributes\n    for a prim to select a corresponding Shader Node Definition (\"Sdr Node\"),\n    as well as to look up a runtime entry for that shader node in the\n    form of an SdrShaderNode.\n\n    UsdShadeNodeDefAPI is intended to be a pre-applied API schema for any\n    prim type that wants to refer to the SdrRegistry for further implementation\n    details about the behavior of that prim.  The primary use in UsdShade\n    itself is as UsdShadeShader, which is a basis for material shading networks\n    (UsdShadeMaterial), but this is intended to be used in other domains\n    that also use the Sdr node mechanism.\n\n    This schema provides properties that allow a prim to identify an external\n    node definition, either by a direct identifier key into the SdrRegistry\n    (info:id), an asset to be parsed by a suitable NdrParserPlugin\n    (info:sourceAsset), or an inline source code that must also be parsed\n    (info:sourceCode); as well as a selector attribute to determine which\n    specifier is active (info:implementationSource).\n    '''\n)\n{\n    uniform token info:id (\n        doc = \"\"\"The id is an identifier for the type or purpose of the \n        shader. E.g.: Texture or FractalFloat.\n        The use of this id will depend on the render context: some will turn it\n        into an actual shader path, some will use it to generate shader source \n        code dynamically.\n        \n        \\\\sa SetShaderId()\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform token info:implementationSource = \"id\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"id\", \"sourceAsset\", \"sourceCode\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Specifies the attribute that should be consulted to get the \n        shader's implementation or its source code.\n\n        * If set to \\\"id\\\", the \\\"info:id\\\" attribute's value is used to \n        determine the shader source from the shader registry.\n        * If set to \\\"sourceAsset\\\", the resolved value of the \\\"info:sourceAsset\\\" \n        attribute corresponding to the desired implementation (or source-type)\n        is used to locate the shader source.  A source asset file may also\n        specify multiple shader definitions, so there is an optional attribute\n        \\\"info:sourceAsset:subIdentifier\\\" whose value should be used to indicate\n        a particular shader definition from a source asset file.\n        * If set to \\\"sourceCode\\\", the value of \\\"info:sourceCode\\\" attribute \n        corresponding to the desired implementation (or source type) is used as \n        the shader source.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"ConnectableAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"UsdShadeConnectableAPI is an API schema that provides a common\n    interface for creating outputs and making connections between shading \n    parameters and outputs. The interface is common to all UsdShade schemas\n    that support Inputs and Outputs, which currently includes UsdShadeShader,\n    UsdShadeNodeGraph, and UsdShadeMaterial .\n\n    One can construct a UsdShadeConnectableAPI directly from a UsdPrim, or\n    from objects of any of the schema classes listed above.  If it seems\n    onerous to need to construct a secondary schema object to interact with\n    Inputs and Outputs, keep in mind that any function whose purpose is either\n    to walk material/shader networks via their connections, or to create such\n    networks, can typically be written entirely in terms of \n    UsdShadeConnectableAPI objects, without needing to care what the underlying\n    prim type is.\n\n    Additionally, the most common UsdShadeConnectableAPI behaviors\n    (creating Inputs and Outputs, and making connections) are wrapped as\n    convenience methods on the prim schema classes (creation) and \n    UsdShadeInput and UsdShadeOutput.\n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n}\n\nclass \"MaterialBindingAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"UsdShadeMaterialBindingAPI is an API schema that provides an \n    interface for binding materials to prims or collections of prims \n    (represented by UsdCollectionAPI objects). \n    \n    In the USD shading model, each renderable gprim computes a single \n    <b>resolved Material</b> that will be used to shade the gprim (exceptions, \n    of course, for gprims that possess UsdGeomSubsets, as each subset can be \n    shaded by a different Material).  A gprim <b>and each of its ancestor \n    prims</b> can possess, through the MaterialBindingAPI, both a \n    <b>direct</b> binding to a Material, and any number of \n    <b>collection-based</b> bindings to Materials; each binding can be generic \n    or declared for a particular <b>purpose</b>, and given a specific <b>binding \n    strength</b>. It is the process of \\\"material resolution\\\" (see \n    that examines all of \n    these bindings, and selects the one Material that best matches the \n    client's needs.\n\n    The intent of <b>purpose</b> is that each gprim should be able to resolve a \n    Material for any given purpose, which implies it can have differently bound \n    materials for different purposes. There are two <i>special</i> values of \n    <b>purpose</b> defined in UsdShade, although the API fully supports \n    specifying arbitrary values for it, for the sake of extensibility:\n    <ul><li><b>UsdShadeTokens->full</b>: to be used when the purpose of the \n    render is entirely to visualize the truest representation of a scene, \n    considering all lighting and material information, at highest fidelity.</li>  \n    <li><b>UsdShadeTokens->preview</b>: to be used when the render is in \n    service of a goal other than a high fidelity \\\"full\\\" render (such as scene\n    manipulation, modeling, or realtime playback). Latency and speed are \n    generally of greater concern for preview renders, therefore preview \n    materials are generally designed to be \\\"lighterweight\\\" compared to full\n    materials.</li></ul>\n    A binding can also have no specific purpose at all, in which \n    case, it is considered to be the fallback or all-purpose binding (denoted \n    by the empty-valued token <b>UsdShadeTokens->allPurpose</b>). \n\n    The <b>purpose</b> of a material binding is encoded in the name of the \n    binding relationship. \n    <ul><li>\n    In the case of a direct binding, the <i>allPurpose</i> binding is \n    represented by the relationship named <b>material:binding</b>. \n    Special-purpose direct bindings are represented by relationships named\n    <b>material:binding:<i>purpose</i></b>. A direct binding relationship \n    must have a single target path that points to a <b>UsdShadeMaterial</b>.</li>\n    <li>\n    In the case of a collection-based binding, the <i>allPurpose</i> binding is \n    represented by a relationship named \n    <b>material:binding:collection:<i>bindingName</i></b>, where \n    <b>bindingName</b> establishes an identity for the binding that is unique \n    on the prim. Attempting to establish two collection bindings of the same \n    name on the same prim will result in the first binding simply being \n    overridden. A special-purpose collection-based binding is represented by a \n    relationship named <b>material:binding:collection:<i>purpose:bindingName</i></b>.\n    A collection-based binding relationship must have exacly two targets, one of \n    which should be a collection-path (see \n    and the other should point to a\n    <b>UsdShadeMaterial</b>. In the future, we may allow a single collection \n    binding to target multiple collections, if we can establish a reasonable \n    round-tripping pattern for applications that only allow a single collection \n    to be associated with each Material.\n    </li>\n    </ul>\n\n    <b>Note:</b> Both <b>bindingName</b> and <b>purpose</b> must be \n    non-namespaced tokens. This allows us to know the role of a binding \n    relationship simply from the number of tokens in it. \n    <ul><li><b>Two tokens</b>: the fallback, \\\"all purpose\\\", direct binding, \n    <i>material:binding</i></li>\n    <li><b>Three tokens</b>: a purpose-restricted, direct, fallback binding, \n    e.g. material:binding:preview</li>\n    <li><b>Four tokens</b>: an all-purpose, collection-based binding, e.g. \n    material:binding:collection:metalBits</li>\n    <li><b>Five tokens</b>: a purpose-restricted, collection-based binding, \n    e.g. material:binding:collection:full:metalBits</li>\n    </ul>\n\n    A <b>binding-strength</b> value is used to specify whether a binding \n    authored on a prim should be weaker or stronger than bindings that appear \n    lower in namespace. We encode the binding strength with as token-valued \n    metadata <b>'bindMaterialAs'</b> for future flexibility, even though for \n    now, there are only two possible values:\n    <i>UsdShadeTokens->weakerThanDescendants</i> and \n    <i>UsdShadeTokens->strongerThanDescendants</i>. When binding-strength is \n    not authored (i.e. empty) on a binding-relationship, the default behavior \n    matches UsdShadeTokens->weakerThanDescendants.\n\n    \\\\note If a material binding relationship is a built-in property defined as \n    part of a typed prim's schema, a fallback value should not be provided for \n    it. This is because the \\\"material resolution\\\" algorithm only conisders \n    <i>authored</i> properties.\n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n}\n\nclass \"CoordSysAPI\" (\n    doc = '''UsdShadeCoordSysAPI provides a way to designate, name,\n    and discover coordinate systems.\n\n    Coordinate systems are implicitly established by UsdGeomXformable\n    prims, using their local space.  That coordinate system may be\n    bound (i.e., named) from another prim.  The binding is encoded\n    as a single-target relationship.\n    Coordinate system bindings apply to descendants of the prim\n    where the binding is expressed, but names may be re-bound by\n    descendant prims.\n\n    CoordSysAPI is a multi-apply API schema, where instance names \n    signify the named coordinate systems. The instance names are\n    used with the \"coordSys:\" namespace to determine the binding\n    to the UsdGeomXformable prim.\n\n    Named coordinate systems are useful in shading (and other) workflows.\n    An example is projection paint, which projects a texture\n    from a certain view (the paint coordinate system), encoded as \n    (e.g.) \"rel coordSys:paint:binding\".  Using the paint coordinate frame \n    avoids the need to assign a UV set to the object, and can be a \n    concise way to project paint across a collection of objects with \n    a single shared paint coordinate system.\n    '''\n)\n{\n    rel coordSys:__INSTANCE_NAME__:binding (\n        displayName = \"Bound Coordinate System\"\n        doc = \"Prim binding expressing the appropriate coordinate systems.\"\n    )\n}\n\n"
- "#usda 1.0\n(\n    \"WARNING: THIS FILE IS GENERATED BY usdGenSchema.  DO NOT EDIT.\"\n)\n\nclass PhysicsScene \"PhysicsScene\" (\n    doc = \"General physics simulation properties, required for simulation.\"\n)\n{\n    vector3f physics:gravityDirection = (0, 0, 0) (\n        displayName = \"Gravity Direction\"\n        doc = \"\"\"Gravity direction vector in simulation world space. Will be\n        normalized before use. A zero vector is a request to use the negative \n        upAxis. Unitless.\"\"\"\n    )\n    float physics:gravityMagnitude = -inf (\n        displayName = \"Gravity Magnitude\"\n        doc = \"\"\"Gravity acceleration magnitude in simulation world space. \n        A negative value is a request to use a value equivalent to earth \n        gravity regardless of the metersPerUnit scaling used by this scene. \n        Units: distance/second/second.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"PhysicsRigidBodyAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"Applies physics body attributes to any UsdGeomXformable prim and\n    marks that prim to be driven by a simulation. A kinematic \n        body is a body that is moved through animated poses or through \n        user defined poses. The simulation derives velocities for the\n        kinematic body based on the external motion. When a continuous motion\n        is not desired, this kinematic flag should be set to false.\"\"\"\n    )\n    bool physics:rigidBodyEnabled = 1 (\n        displayName = \"Rigid Body Enabled\"\n        doc = \"Determines if this PhysicsRigidBodyAPI is enabled.\"\n    )\n    rel physics:simulationOwner (\n        displayName = \"Simulation Owner\"\n        doc = \"\"\"Single PhysicsScene that will simulate this body. By \n        default this is the first PhysicsScene found in the stage using \n        UsdStage::Traverse().\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform bool physics:startsAsleep = 0 (\n        displayName = \"Starts as Asleep\"\n        doc = \"Determines if the body is asleep when the simulation starts.\"\n    )\n    vector3f physics:velocity = (0, 0, 0) (\n        displayName = \"Linear Velocity\"\n        doc = \"\"\"Linear velocity in the same space as the node's xform. \n        Units: distance/second.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"PhysicsMassAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"Defines explicit mass properties (mass, density, inertia etc.).        \n    MassAPI can be applied to any object that has a PhysicsCollisionAPI or\n    a PhysicsRigidBodyAPI.\"\"\"\n)\n{\n    point3f physics:centerOfMass = (-inf, -inf, -inf) (\n        displayName = \"Center of Mass\"\n        doc = \"Center of mass in the prim's local space. Units: distance.\"\n    )\n    float physics:density = 0 (\n        displayName = \"Density\"\n        doc = \"\"\"If non-zero, specifies the density of the object.\n        In the context of rigid body physics, density indirectly results in \n        setting mass via (mass = density x volume of the object). How the \n        volume is computed is up to implementation of the physics system.\n        It is generally computed from the collision approximation rather than\n        the graphical mesh. In the case where both density and mass are \n        specified for the same object, mass has precedence over density. \n        Unlike mass, child's prim's density overrides parent prim's density \n        as it is accumulative. Note that density of a collisionAPI can be also\n        alternatively set through a PhysicsMaterialAPI. The material density\n        has the weakest precedence in density definition. Note if density is\n        0.0 it is ignored. Units: mass/distance/distance/distance.\"\"\"\n    )\n    float3 physics:diagonalInertia = (0, 0, 0) (\n        displayName = \"Diagonal Inertia\"\n        doc = \"\"\"If non-zero, specifies diagonalized inertia tensor along the \n        principal axes. Note if diagonalInertial is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0) it is \n        ignored. Units: mass*distance*distance.\"\"\"\n    )\n    float physics:mass = 0 (\n        displayName = \"Mass\"\n        doc = \"\"\"If non-zero, directly specifies the mass of the object.\n        Note that any child prim can also have a mass when they apply massAPI.\n        In this case, the precedence rule is 'parent mass overrides the\n        child's'. This may come as counter-intuitive, but mass is a computed \n        quantity and in general not accumulative. For example, if a parent \n        has mass of 10, and one of two children has mass of 20, allowing \n        child's mass to override its parent results in a mass of -10 for the \n        other child. Note if mass is 0.0 it is ignored. Units: mass.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    quatf physics:principalAxes = (0, 0, 0, 0) (\n        displayName = \"Principal Axes\"\n        doc = \"\"\"Orientation of the inertia tensor's principal axes in the \n        prim's local space.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"PhysicsCollisionAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"Applies collision attributes to a UsdGeomXformable prim. If a \n    simulation is running, this geometry will collide with other geometries that \n    have PhysicsCollisionAPI applied. If a prim in the parent hierarchy has the\n    RigidBodyAPI applied, this collider is a part of that body. If there is \n    no body in the parent hierarchy, this collider is considered to be static.\"\"\"\n)\n{\n    bool physics:collisionEnabled = 1 (\n        displayName = \"Collision Enabled\"\n        doc = \"Determines if the PhysicsCollisionAPI is enabled.\"\n    )\n    rel physics:simulationOwner (\n        displayName = \"Simulation Owner\"\n        doc = \"\"\"Single PhysicsScene that will simulate this collider. \n        By default this object belongs to the first PhysicsScene.\n        Note that if a RigidBodyAPI in the hierarchy above has a different\n        simulationOwner then it has a precedence over this relationship.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"PhysicsMeshCollisionAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"Attributes to control how a Mesh is made into a collider.\n       Can be applied to only a USDGeomMesh in addition to its\n       PhysicsCollisionAPI.\"\"\"\n)\n{\n    uniform token physics:approximation = \"none\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"none\", \"convexDecomposition\", \"convexHull\", \"boundingSphere\", \"boundingCube\", \"meshSimplification\"]\n        displayName = \"Approximation\"\n        doc = \"\"\"Determines the mesh's collision approximation:\n\\t\\\"none\\\" - The mesh geometry is used directly as a collider without any \n    approximation.\n\\t\\\"convexDecomposition\\\" - A convex mesh decomposition is performed. This \n    results in a set of convex mesh colliders.\n\\t\\\"convexHull\\\" - A convex hull of the mesh is generated and used as the \n    collider.\n\\t\\\"boundingSphere\\\" - A bounding sphere is computed around the mesh and used \n    as a collider.\n\\t\\\"boundingCube\\\" - An optimally fitting box collider is computed around the \n    mesh.\n\\t\\\"meshSimplification\\\" - A mesh simplification step is performed, resulting \n    in a simplified triangle mesh collider.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"PhysicsMaterialAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\" Adds simulation material properties to a Material. All collisions \n    that have a relationship to this material will have their collision response \n    defined through this material.\"\"\"\n)\n{\n    float physics:density = 0 (\n        displayName = \"Density\"\n        doc = \"\"\"If non-zero, defines the density of the material. This can be\n        used for body mass computation, see PhysicsMassAPI.\n        Note that if the density is 0.0 it is ignored. \n        Units: mass/distance/distance/distance.\"\"\"\n    )\n    float physics:dynamicFriction = 0 (\n        displayName = \"Dynamic Friction\"\n        doc = \"Dynamic friction coefficient. Unitless.\"\n    )\n    float physics:restitution = 0 (\n        displayName = \"Restitution\"\n        doc = \"Restitution coefficient. Unitless.\"\n    )\n    float physics:staticFriction = 0 (\n        displayName = \"Static Friction\"\n        doc = \"Static friction coefficient. Unitless.\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass PhysicsCollisionGroup \"PhysicsCollisionGroup\" (\n    apiSchemas = [\"CollectionAPI:colliders\"]\n    doc = \"\"\"Defines a collision group for coarse filtering. However, if this option is set, the filter will disable\n        collisions against all colliders except for those in the selected filter\n        groups.\"\"\"\n    )\n    string physics:mergeGroup (\n        displayName = \"Merge With Groups\"\n        doc = \"\"\"If non-empty, any collision groups in a stage with a matching\n        mergeGroup should be considered to refer to the same collection. Matching\n        collision groups should behave as if there were a single group containing\n        referenced colliders and filter groups from both collections.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"PhysicsFilteredPairsAPI\" (\n    doc = '''API to describe fine-grained filtering. Note that FilteredPairsAPI filtering has precedence \n    over CollisionGroup filtering.'''\n)\n{\n    rel physics:filteredPairs (\n        displayName = \"Filtered Pairs\"\n        doc = \"Relationship to objects that should be filtered.\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass PhysicsJoint \"PhysicsJoint\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"A joint constrains the movement of rigid bodies. This is entirely optional, but can be\n        useful in several scenarios:\n        \n        - In a pipeline that does pruning (for complexity management)\n        by deactivating prims composed from asset references, when we\n        deactivate a purpose=\"render\" prim, we will be able to discover\n        and additionally deactivate its associated purpose=\"proxy\" prim,\n        so that preview renders reflect the pruning accurately.\n        \n        - DCC importers may be able to make more aggressive optimizations\n        for interactive processing and display if they can discover the proxy\n        for a given render prim.\n        \n        - With a little more work, a Hydra-based application will be able\n        to map a picked proxy prim back to its render geometry for selection.\n\n        \\\\note It is only valid to author the proxyPrim relationship on\n        prims whose purpose is \"render\".'''\n    )\n    uniform token purpose = \"default\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"default\", \"render\", \"proxy\", \"guide\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Purpose is a classification of geometry into categories that \n        can each be independently included or excluded from traversals of prims \n        on a stage, such as rendering or bounding-box computation traversals.\n\n        See for more detail about how \n        purpose is computed and used.\"\"\"\n    )\n    token visibility = \"inherited\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"inherited\", \"invisible\"]\n        doc = '''Visibility is meant to be the simplest form of \"pruning\" \n        visibility that is supported by most DCC apps. Array length should match the size of the \n        *joints* attribute.\"\"\"\n    )\n    half3[] scales (\n        doc = \"\"\"Joint-local scales of all affected joints, in\n        16 bit precision. Array length should match the size of the *joints* \n        attribute.\"\"\"\n    )\n    float3[] translations (\n        doc = \"\"\"Joint-local translations of all affected joints. Array length \n        should match the size of the *joints* attribute.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"SkelBindingAPI\" (\n    doc = '''Provides API for authoring and extracting all the skinning-related\n    data that lives in the \"geometry hierarchy\" of prims and models that want\n    to be skeletally deformed.\n\n    See the extended \"UsdSkelBindingAPI schema\"\n    documentation for more about bindings and how they apply in a scene graph.\n    '''\n)\n{\n    matrix4d primvars:skel:geomBindTransform (\n        doc = '''Encodes the bind-time world space transforms of the prim.\n        If the transform is identical for a group of gprims that share a common\n        ancestor, the transform may be authored on the ancestor, to \"inherit\"\n        down to all the leaf gprims. If this transform is unset, an identity\n        transform is used instead.'''\n    )\n    int[] primvars:skel:jointIndices (\n        doc = \"\"\"Indices into the *joints* attribute of the closest\n        (in namespace) bound Skeleton that affect each point of a PointBased\n        gprim. The primvar can have either *constant* or *vertex* interpolation.\n        This primvar's *elementSize* will determine how many joint influences\n        apply to each point. Indices must point be valid. Null influences should\n        be defined by setting values in jointWeights to zero.\n        See UsdGeomPrimvar for more information on interpolation and\n        elementSize.\"\"\"\n    )\n    float[] primvars:skel:jointWeights (\n        doc = \"\"\"Weights for the joints that affect each point of a PointBased\n        gprim. The primvar can have either *constant* or *vertex* interpolation.\n        This primvar's *elementSize* will determine how many joints influences\n        apply to each point. The length, interpolation, and elementSize of\n        *jointWeights* must match that of *jointIndices*. See UsdGeomPrimvar\n        for more information on interpolation and elementSize.\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform token primvars:skel:skinningMethod = \"classicLinear\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"classicLinear\", \"dualQuaternion\"]\n        doc = \"The skinningMethod specifies the skinning method for the prim.\"\n    )\n    rel skel:animationSource (\n        doc = \"\"\"Animation source to be bound to Skeleton primitives at or\n        beneath the location at which this property is defined.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform token[] skel:blendShapes (\n        doc = \"\"\"An array of tokens defining the order onto which blend shape\n        weights from an animation source map onto the *skel:blendShapeTargets*\n        rel of a binding site. If authored, the number of elements must be equal\n        to the number of targets in the _blendShapeTargets_ rel. This property\n        is not inherited hierarchically, and is expected to be authored directly\n        on the skinnable primitive to which the blend shapes apply.\"\"\"\n    )\n    rel skel:blendShapeTargets (\n        doc = \"\"\"Ordered list of all target blend shapes. This property is not\n        inherited hierarchically, and is expected to be authored directly on\n        the skinnable primitive to which the the blend shapes apply.\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform token[] skel:joints (\n        doc = \"\"\"An (optional) array of tokens defining the list of\n        joints to which jointIndices apply. If undefined on a primitive, the primitive inherits the \n        value of the nearest ancestor prim, if any.\"\"\"\n    )\n    rel skel:skeleton (\n        doc = \"\"\"Skeleton to be bound to this prim and its descendents that\n        possess a mapping and weighting to the joints of the identified\n        Skeleton.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass BlendShape \"BlendShape\" (\n    doc = '''Describes a target blend shape, possibly containing inbetween\n      shapes.\n\n      See the extended \"Blend Shape Schema\n      documentation for information.\n      '''\n)\n{\n    uniform vector3f[] normalOffsets (\n        doc = \"\"\"**Required property**. Normal offsets which, when added to the\n        base pose, provides the normals of the target shape.\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform vector3f[] offsets (\n        doc = \"\"\"**Required property**. If\n        authored, the number of elements must be equal to the number of elements\n        in the *offsets* array.\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\n"
- "#usda 1.0\n(\n    \"WARNING: THIS FILE IS GENERATED BY usdGenSchema.  DO NOT EDIT.\"\n)\n\nclass SpatialAudio \"SpatialAudio\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"The SpatialAudio primitive defines basic properties for encoding \n    playback of an audio file or stream within a USD Stage. The SpatialAudio \n    schema derives from UsdGeomXformable since it can support full spatial \n    audio while also supporting non-spatial mono and stereo sounds. One or \n    more SpatialAudio prims can be placed anywhere in the namespace, though it \n    is advantageous to place truly spatial audio prims under/inside the models \n    from which the sound emanates, so that the audio prim need only be \n    transformed relative to the model, rather than copying its animation.\n\n    Timecode Attributes and Time Scaling\n    \\\\a startTime and \\\\a endTime are \\\"timecode\\\" valued \n    attributes which gives them the special behavior that \n    \\\"layer offsets\\\" affecting the layer in \n    which one of these values is authored are applied to the attribute's value \n    itself during value resolution. This allows audio playback to be kept in \n    sync with time sampled animation as the animation is affected by \n    \\\"layer offsets\\\" in the composition. But this behavior \n    brings with it some interesting edge cases and caveats when it comes to \n    \\\"layer offsets\\\" that include scale.\n\n    ####  Layer Offsets do not affect Media Dilation\n    Although authored layer offsets may have a time scale which can scale the\n    duration between an authored \\\\a startTime and \\\\a endTime, we make no \n    attempt to infer any playback dilation of the actual audio media itself. \n    Given that \\\\a startTime and \\\\a endTime can be independently authored in \n    different layers with differing time scales, it is not possible, in general,\n    to define an \\\"original timeframe\\\" from which we can compute a dilation to \n    composed stage-time. Even if we could compute a composed dilation this way,\n    it would still be impossible to flatten a stage or layer stack into a single\n    layer and still retain the composed audio dilation using this schema.\n\n    #### Inverting startTime and endTime\n    Although we do not expect it to be common, it is possible to apply a \n    negative time scale to USD layers, which mostly has the effect of reversing\n    animation in the affected composition. If a negative scale is applied to a\n    composition that contains authored \\\\a startTime and \\\\a endTime, it will\n    reverse their relative ordering in time. Therefore, we stipulate when\n    \\\\a playbackMode is \\\"onceFromStartToEnd\\\" or \\\"loopFromStartToEnd\\\", if \n    \\\\a endTime is less than \\\\a startTime, then begin playback at \\\\a endTime, \n    and continue until \\\\a startTime. When \\\\a startTime and \\\\a endTime are \n    inverted, we do not, however, stipulate that playback of the audio media \n    itself be inverted, since doing so \\\"successfully\\\" would require perfect \n    knowledge of when, within the audio clip, relevant audio ends (so that we \n    know how to offset the reversed audio to align it so that we reach the \n    \\\"beginning\\\" at \\\\a startTime), and sounds played in reverse are not likely \n    to produce desirable results. \n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n    uniform token auralMode = \"spatial\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"spatial\", \"nonSpatial\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Determines how audio should be played.\n        Valid values are:\n        - spatial: Play the audio in 3D space if the device can support spatial\n          audio. if not, fall back to mono.\n        - nonSpatial: Play the audio without regard to the SpatialAudio prim's \n          position. If the audio media contains any form of stereo or other \n          multi-channel sound, it is left to the application to determine \n          whether the listener's position should be taken into account. We \n          expect nonSpatial to be the choice for ambient sounds and music \n          sound-tracks.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform timecode endTime = 0 (\n        doc = \"\"\"Expressed in the timeCodesPerSecond of the containing stage, \n        \\\\a endTime specifies when the audio stream will cease playing during \n        animation playback if the length of the referenced audio clip is \n        longer than desired. This only applies if \\\\a playbackMode is set to \n        onceFromStartToEnd or loopFromStartToEnd, otherwise the \\\\a endTimeCode \n        of the stage is used instead of \\\\a endTime.\n        If \\\\a endTime is less than \\\\a startTime, it is expected that the audio \n        will instead be played from \\\\a endTime to \\\\a startTime.\n        Note that \\\\a endTime is expressed as a timecode so that the stage can \n        properly apply layer offsets when resolving its value.\n        See for more details and caveats.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform asset filePath = @@ (\n        doc = '''Path to the audio file.\n        In general, the formats allowed for audio files is no more constrained \n        by USD than is image-type. As with images, however, usdz has stricter \n        requirements based on DMA and format support in browsers and consumer \n        devices. The allowed audio filetypes for usdz are M4A, MP3, WAV \n        (in order of preference).\n        \\\\sa <a href=\"https://openusd.org/release/spec_usdz.html\">Usdz Specification</a>\n        '''\n    )\n    double gain = 1 (\n        doc = '''Multiplier on the incoming audio signal. A value of 0 \"mutes\" \n        the signal. Negative values will be clamped to 0. \n        '''\n    )\n    uniform double mediaOffset = 0 (\n        doc = \"\"\"Expressed in seconds, \\\\a mediaOffset specifies the offset from \n        the referenced audio file's beginning at which we should begin playback \n        when stage playback reaches the time that prim's audio should start.\n        If the prim's \\\\a playbackMode is a looping mode, \\\\a mediaOffset is \n        applied only to the first run-through of the audio clip; the second and \n        all other loops begin from the start of the audio clip.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform token playbackMode = \"onceFromStart\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"onceFromStart\", \"onceFromStartToEnd\", \"loopFromStart\", \"loopFromStartToEnd\", \"loopFromStage\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Along with \\\\a startTime and \\\\a endTime, determines when the \n        audio playback should start and stop during the stage's animation \n        playback and whether the audio should loop during its duration. \n        Valid values are:\n        - onceFromStart: Play the audio once, starting at \\\\a startTime, \n          continuing until the audio completes.\n        - onceFromStartToEnd: Play the audio once beginning at \\\\a startTime, \n          continuing until \\\\a endTime or until the audio completes, whichever \n          comes first.\n        - loopFromStart: Start playing the audio at \\\\a startTime and continue \n          looping through to the stage's authored \\\\a endTimeCode.\n        - loopFromStartToEnd: Start playing the audio at \\\\a startTime and \n          continue looping through, stopping the audio at \\\\a endTime.\n        - loopFromStage: Start playing the audio at the stage's authored \n          \\\\a startTimeCode and continue looping through to the stage's authored \n          \\\\a endTimeCode. This can be useful for ambient sounds that should always \n          be active.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    rel proxyPrim (\n        doc = '''The proxyPrim relationship allows us to link a\n        prim whose purpose is \"render\" to its (single target)\n        purpose=\"proxy\" prim.  This is entirely optional, but can be\n        useful in several scenarios:\n        \n        - In a pipeline that does pruning (for complexity management)\n        by deactivating prims composed from asset references, when we\n        deactivate a purpose=\"render\" prim, we will be able to discover\n        and additionally deactivate its associated purpose=\"proxy\" prim,\n        so that preview renders reflect the pruning accurately.\n        \n        - DCC importers may be able to make more aggressive optimizations\n        for interactive processing and display if they can discover the proxy\n        for a given render prim.\n        \n        - With a little more work, a Hydra-based application will be able\n        to map a picked proxy prim back to its render geometry for selection.\n\n        \\\\note It is only valid to author the proxyPrim relationship on\n        prims whose purpose is \"render\".'''\n    )\n    uniform token purpose = \"default\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"default\", \"render\", \"proxy\", \"guide\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Purpose is a classification of geometry into categories that \n        can each be independently included or excluded from traversals of prims \n        on a stage, such as rendering or bounding-box computation traversals.\n\n        See for more detail about how \n        purpose is computed and used.\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform timecode startTime = 0 (\n        doc = \"\"\"Expressed in the timeCodesPerSecond of the containing stage, \n        \\\\a startTime specifies when the audio stream will start playing during \n        animation playback. This value is ignored when \\\\a playbackMode is set \n        to loopFromStage as, in this mode, the audio will always start at the \n        stage's authored \\\\a startTimeCode.\n        Note that \\\\a startTime is expressed as a timecode so that the stage can \n        properly apply layer offsets when resolving its value. See \n        for more details and caveats.\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    token visibility = \"inherited\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"inherited\", \"invisible\"]\n        doc = '''Visibility is meant to be the simplest form of \"pruning\" \n        visibility that is supported by most DCC apps.  Visibility is \n        animatable, allowing a sub-tree of geometry to be present for some \n        segment of a shot, and absent from others; unlike the action of \n        deactivating geometry prims, invisible geometry is still \n        available for inspection, for positioning, for defining volumes, etc.'''\n    )\n    uniform token[] xformOpOrder (\n        doc = \"\"\"Encodes the sequence of transformation operations in the\n        order in which they should be pushed onto a transform stack while\n        visiting a UsdStage's prims in a graph traversal that will effect\n        the desired positioning for this prim and its descendant prims.\n        \n        You should rarely, if ever, need to manipulate this attribute directly.\n        It is managed by the AddXformOp(), SetResetXformStack(), and\n        SetXformOpOrder(), and consulted by GetOrderedXformOps() and\n        GetLocalTransformation().\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"AssetPreviewsAPI\" (\n    doc = \"\"\"AssetPreviewsAPI is the interface for authoring and accessing \n    precomputed, lightweight previews of assets.  It is an applied schema, \n    which means that an arbitrary number of prims on a stage can have the schema \n    applied and therefore can contain previews; however, to access a stage's \n    \\\"default\\\" previews, one consults \n    the stage's `defaultPrim`.\n    \n    AssetPreviewsAPI supports the following kinds of previews:\n    - **thumbnails** : a set of pre-rendered images of the asset.  There is no \n      prescribed size for thumbnail images, but care should be taken to ensure\n      their inclusion does not substantially increase the overall size of an\n      asset, as, for example, when packaged into USDZ.\n    \n    Although the UsdMediaAssetPreviewsAPI class can be used to interrogate any\n    prim, no query in the API will succeed unless the schema has been applied\n    to the prim.  This schema deals only with asset paths, and clients wishing\n    to directly consume the returned data must do so by retrieving an ArAsset\n    from the session's ArAssetResolver.\n    \n    The schema defines no properties or metadata fallback values.  Rather, \n    Asset Previews are encoded as part of a prim's `assetInfo` metadata.  A \n    default thumbnail image would look like:\n    ```\n1.    assetInfo = {\n2.      dictionary previews = {\n3.          dictionary thumbnails = {\n4.              dictionary default = {\n5.                  asset defaultImage = @chair_thumb.jpg@\n6.              }\n7.          }\n8.      }\n9.    }\n    ```\n\n    \"\"\"\n)\n{\n}\n\n"
- "#usda 1.0\n(\n    \"WARNING: THIS FILE IS GENERATED BY usdGenSchema.  DO NOT EDIT.\"\n)\n\nclass Volume \"Volume\" (\n    customData = {\n        string userDocBrief = \"\"\"A renderable volume containing one or more\nvolumetric data fields, used to represent a volume effect such as smoke or fire.\"\"\"\n    }\n    doc = \"\"\"A renderable volume primitive. A volume is made up of any number\n             of FieldBase primitives bound together in this volume. Each\n             FieldBase primitive is specified as a relationship with a\n             namespace prefix of \\\"field\\\".\n\n             The relationship name is used by the renderer to associate\n             individual fields with the named input parameters on the volume\n             shader. Using this indirect approach to connecting fields to\n             shader parameters (rather than using the field prim's name)\n             allows a single field to be reused for different shader inputs, or\n             to be used as different shader parameters when rendering different\n             Volumes. This means that the name of the field prim is not\n             relevant to its contribution to the volume prims which refer to\n             it. Nor does the field prim's location in the scene graph have\n             any relevance, and Volumes may refer to fields anywhere in the\n             scene graph.  **However**, unless Field prims need to be shared\n             by multiple Volumes, a Volume's Field prims should be located\n             under the Volume in namespace, for enhanced organization.\"\"\"\n)\n{\n    uniform bool doubleSided = 0 (\n        doc = \"\"\"Although some renderers treat all parametric or polygonal\n        surfaces as if they were effectively laminae with outward-facing\n        normals on both sides, some renderers derive significant optimizations\n        by considering these surfaces to have only a single outward side,\n        typically determined by control-point winding order and/or \n        orientation.  By doing so they can perform \\\"backface culling\\\" to\n        avoid drawing the many polygons of most closed surfaces that face away\n        from the viewer.\n        \n        However, it is often advantageous to model thin objects such as paper\n        and cloth as single, open surfaces that must be viewable from both\n        sides, always.  Setting a gprim's doubleSided attribute to \n        \\\\c true instructs all renderers to disable optimizations such as\n        backface culling for the gprim, and attempt (not all renderers are able\n        to do so, but the USD reference GL renderer always will) to provide\n        forward-facing normals on each side of the surface for lighting\n        calculations.\"\"\"\n    )\n    float3[] extent (\n        doc = \"\"\"Extent is a three dimensional range measuring the geometric\n        extent of the authored gprim in its own local space (i.e. its own\n        transform not applied), without accounting for any shader-induced\n        displacement. If __any__ extent value has been authored for a given \n        Boundable, then it should be authored at every timeSample at which \n        geometry-affecting properties are authored, to ensure correct \n        evaluation via ComputeExtent(). If __no__ extent value has been \n        authored, then ComputeExtent() will call the Boundable's registered \n        ComputeExtentFunction(), which may be expensive, which is why we \n        strongly encourage proper authoring of extent.\n        \\\\sa ComputeExtent()\n        \\\\sa \\\\ref UsdGeom_Boundable_Extent.\n        \n        An authored extent on a prim which has children is expected to include\n        the extent of all children, as they will be pruned from BBox computation\n        during traversal.\"\"\"\n    )\n    uniform token orientation = \"rightHanded\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"rightHanded\", \"leftHanded\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Orientation specifies whether the gprim's surface normal \n        should be computed using the right hand rule, or the left hand rule.\n        Please see for a deeper explanation and\n        generalization of orientation to composed scenes with transformation\n        hierarchies.\"\"\"\n    )\n    color3f[] primvars:displayColor (\n        doc = '''It is useful to have an \"official\" colorSet that can be used\n        as a display or modeling color, even in the absence of any specified\n        shader for a gprim.  DisplayColor serves this role; because it is a\n        UsdGeomPrimvar, it can also be used as a gprim override for any shader\n        that consumes a displayColor parameter.'''\n    )\n    float[] primvars:displayOpacity (\n        doc = \"\"\"Companion to displayColor that specifies opacity, broken\n        out as an independent attribute rather than an rgba color, both so that\n        each can be independently overridden, and because shaders rarely consume\n        rgba parameters.\"\"\"\n    )\n    rel proxyPrim (\n        doc = '''The proxyPrim relationship allows us to link a\n        prim whose purpose is \"render\" to its (single target)\n        purpose=\"proxy\" prim.  This is entirely optional, but can be\n        useful in several scenarios:\n        \n        - In a pipeline that does pruning (for complexity management)\n        by deactivating prims composed from asset references, when we\n        deactivate a purpose=\"render\" prim, we will be able to discover\n        and additionally deactivate its associated purpose=\"proxy\" prim,\n        so that preview renders reflect the pruning accurately.\n        \n        - DCC importers may be able to make more aggressive optimizations\n        for interactive processing and display if they can discover the proxy\n        for a given render prim.\n        \n        - With a little more work, a Hydra-based application will be able\n        to map a picked proxy prim back to its render geometry for selection.\n\n        \\\\note It is only valid to author the proxyPrim relationship on\n        prims whose purpose is \"render\".'''\n    )\n    uniform token purpose = \"default\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"default\", \"render\", \"proxy\", \"guide\"]\n        doc = \"\"\"Purpose is a classification of geometry into categories that \n        can each be independently included or excluded from traversals of prims \n        on a stage, such as rendering or bounding-box computation traversals.\n\n        See for more detail about how \n        purpose is computed and used.\"\"\"\n    )\n    token visibility = \"inherited\" (\n        allowedTokens = [\"inherited\", \"invisible\"]\n        doc = '''Visibility is meant to be the simplest form of \"pruning\" \n        visibility that is supported by most DCC apps.  Visibility is \n        animatable, allowing a sub-tree of geometry to be present for some \n        segment of a shot, and absent from others; unlike the action of \n        deactivating geometry prims, invisible geometry is still \n        available for inspection, for positioning, for defining volumes, etc.'''\n    )\n    uniform token[] xformOpOrder (\n        doc = \"\"\"Encodes the sequence of transformation operations in the\n        order in which they should be pushed onto a transform stack while\n        visiting a UsdStage's prims in a graph traversal that will effect\n        the desired positioning for this prim and its descendant prims.\n        \n        You should rarely, if ever, need to manipulate this attribute directly.\n        It is managed by the AddXformOp(), SetResetXformStack(), and\n        SetXformOpOrder(), and consulted by GetOrderedXformOps() and\n        GetLocalTransformation().\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"FieldBase\" (\n    customData = {\n        string userDocBrief = \"The base schema class for volume field primitives.\"\n    }\n    doc = \"Base class for field primitives.\"\n)\n{\n    rel proxyPrim (\n        doc = '''The proxyPrim relationship allows us to link a\n        prim whose purpose is \"render\" to its (single target)\n        purpose=\"proxy\" prim. Visibility is \n        animatable, allowing a sub-tree of geometry to be present for some \n        segment of a shot, and absent from others; unlike the action of \n        deactivating geometry prims, invisible geometry is still \n        available for inspection, for positioning, for defining volumes, etc.'''\n    )\n    uniform token[] xformOpOrder (\n        doc = \"\"\"Encodes the sequence of transformation operations in the\n        order in which they should be pushed onto a transform stack while\n        visiting a UsdStage's prims in a graph traversal that will effect\n        the desired positioning for this prim and its descendant prims.\n        \n        You should rarely, if ever, need to manipulate this attribute directly.\n        It is managed by the AddXformOp(), SetResetXformStack(), and\n        SetXformOpOrder(), and consulted by GetOrderedXformOps() and\n        GetLocalTransformation().\"\"\"\n    )\n}\n\nclass \"FieldAsset\" (\n    customData = {\n        string userDocBrief = \"\"\"The base schema class for volume field \nprimitives defined by an external file.\"\"\"\n    }\n    doc = \"Base class for field primitives defined by an external file.\"\n)\n{\n    token fieldDataType (\n        customData = {\n            string userDocBrief = \"\"\"Token used to indicate the data type of an\nindividual field\"\"\"\n        }\n        doc = \"\"\"Token which is used to indicate the data type of an\n                 individual field. The list of \n                 allowed tokens is specified with the specific asset type. \n                 A missing value is considered an error.\"\"\"\n    )\n    int fieldIndex (\n        customData = {\n            string userDocBrief = \"\"\"Optional attribute that stores an index used \nto disambiguate between fields with the same name.\"\"\"\n        }\n        doc = \"\"\"A file can contain multiple fields with the same\n                 name. This optional attribute is an index used to\n                 disambiguate between these multiple fields with the same\n                 name.\"\"\"\n    )\n    token fieldName (\n        customData = {\n            string userDocBrief = \"\"\"Name of an individual field within the file \nspecified by the filePath attribute.\"\"\"\n        }\n        doc = \"\"\"Name of an individual field within the file specified by\n                 the filePath attribute.\"\"\"\n    )\n    asset filePath (\n        customData = {\n            string userDocBrief = \"An asset path attribute that points to a file on disk.\"\n        }\n        doc = \"\"\"An asset path attribute that points to a file on disk.\n                 For each supported file format, a separate FieldAsset\n                 subclass is required. \n                  \n                 This attribute's value can be animated over time, as most\n                 volume asset formats represent just a single timeSample of\n                 a volume. Container-like prims include Material, NodeGraph, Light, LightFilter. Shader is not a Container-like prim.\"\n                    }, \n                    \"MaterialBindingApiAppliedValidator\": {\n                        \"doc\": \"Verify a prim has the MaterialBindingAPI applied if it has a material binding relationship.\"\n                    }, \n                    \"MaterialBindingCollectionValidator\": {\n                        \"doc\": \"Verify that a collection defining a material binding is well-formed\", \n                        \"schemaTypes\": [\n                            \"MaterialBindingAPI\"\n                        ]\n                    }, \n                    \"MaterialBindingRelationships\": {\n                        \"doc\": \"All properties named 'material:binding' or in that namespace should be relationships.\"\n                    },\n                    \"NormalMapTextureValidator\" : {\n                        \"doc\": \"UsdUVTexture nodes that feed the _inputs:normals_ of a UsdPreviewSurface must ensure that the data is encoded and scaled properly. Specifically, since normals are expected to be in the range [(-1,-1,-1), (1,1,1)], the Texture node must transform 8-bit textures from their [0..1] range by setting its _inputs:scale_ to (2, 2, 2, 1) and _inputs:bias_ to (-1, -1, -1, 0).
